documents: Corell, Estrela & Valiente (2023), Seasonal behaviour and influence of altitude on fog-water collection in the Eastern Iberian Peninsula (2003–2012), Int J Climatol 43:1935–1954 (published PDF)

entry.evidence: In the Iberian Peninsula, a study about the seasonal frequency of fog collection was carried out, but only with a 1-year fog data series

sequences.source_document: Corell et al. 2023, Int J Climatol 43:1935–1954 (published PDF)

steps.action: Frame three questions from regional water scarcity and the short prior record: seasonal behaviour of fog-water collection, collection potential on dry days, and the influence of altitude on volume and frequency.
steps.quote: the present work continues the research line on fog-water collection in the east of the Iberian Peninsula

steps.action: Take from published studies in Chile, Morocco and California the expectation that altitude strongly controls fog-water capture.
steps.quote: Altitude is a proven key factor in fog-water collection.

steps.action: Use the 23-station network of cylindrical passive omnidirectional fog collectors (ASRC-based) with meteorological sensors, built and described in the authors' earlier papers.
steps.quote: Data were obtained via the network of fog-water collectors described in Estrela et al. (2019).

steps.action: Calculate the capture ratio between nylon-thread and Raschel-mesh collectors and convert all data to the reference collector type.
steps.quote: The ratio between the volume captured by the two collection material types was calculated and all data were converted

steps.action: Apply the rain-contribution filter (depending on rain, wind speed and fog) from earlier work to derive the daily fog variable, using a 75% data completeness rule.
steps.quote: This filter has been described in detail by Estrela et al. (2008)

steps.action: Define the analysis variables: meteorological seasons, seasonal collection rate, CV for the longest series, 13 daily intensity bins, and dry days set at a 1 mm threshold above the sensor resolution.
steps.quote: a decision was made to set the limit of 1 mm of precipitation, even though the rain sensor's resolution is lower

steps.action: Design a paired-site comparison: at Mount Montseny and Mount Muela install collector pairs with similar terrain orientation and wind exposure that differ mainly in elevation (398 m and 92 m).
steps.quote: To learn how site elevation influences fog-water collection, the same experiment was run at two different locations specifically.

steps.action: Select three further areas of nearby collectors with similar exposure and overlapping operation periods (southern, central coastal, central inland) for the same elevation comparison.
steps.quote: an analysis similar to the one carried out at Mount Montseny and Mount Muela was conducted in some areas where there were nearby collectors

steps.action: Compute and describe seasonal fog-collection rate time series for all collectors, 2003–2012 (Figure 5): spring and autumn peaks, winter and summer lows, no significant trends.
steps.quote: The sawtooth shape of the series indicates the existence of seasonal variability

steps.action: Compute seasonal mean rates and coefficients of variation for the eight longest-record stations (Figure 6): spring has the highest CV, summer the lowest.
steps.quote: To analyse the consistency of the seasonal values, Figure 6 shows CV values

steps.action: Compute the percentage of fog-collection days and the frequency-intensity distributions by season (Figure 7): summer and autumn have the most fog days, low-intensity days dominate.
steps.quote: the most frequent days with fog were those with low intensities

steps.action: Compute seasonal percentages of fog days with no rain (<1 mm) and seasonal maximum daily dry-day captures for all 23 stations (Figures 8, 9).
steps.quote: the seasonal period with the most days with fog and no rain (<1 mm) was summer

steps.action: Compare accumulated volumes and fog days between upper and lower collectors at Montseny and Muela (Figure 10): about sixfold and twofold more volume, 73% and 61% more days, largest in summer.
steps.quote: At Mount Montseny, the collector located at a higher altitude collected almost sixfold more water than its pair

steps.action: Repeat the elevation comparison at the three additional areas (Figure 11): higher sites collect more volume, but the lowest southern site (Peñones) has the most fog days.
steps.quote: the upper station (Cinto Cabra [9]) collected almost 40% more fog-water than the lower one (Bujete [8])

steps.action: Compute upper-to-lower seasonal ratios of volume and fog days at Montseny and Muela (Figure 12): the largest ratios occur in summer.
steps.quote: Major differences appear that are seasonally dependent.

steps.action: Set the collection rates and dry-day maxima against published values from Peru, Oman, the Canary Islands, Croatia, South Africa and Tenerife.
steps.quote: When comparing these values to those obtained in other places of the world, they were very high

steps.action: Explain the frequent summer and early-autumn fog by the Azores High anticyclone, warm Mediterranean SST and orographic fog formation, drawing on cited work.
steps.quote: this anticyclone situation favours the presence of orographic fog (Corell et al., 2020)

steps.action: Restrict the altitude claim: fog-day frequency is less altitude-dependent than volume, attributed to earlier dissipation and lower liquid water content at low sites; recommend sites above 500 m and about 1,200 m in the north.
steps.quote: it has been observed that the frequency of days with fog collection is not so influenced by altitude

steps.action: Retain altitude as the main differentiating factor between nearby collectors, with summer-amplified differences, alongside the seasonal and dry-day findings.
steps.quote: This study compared sampling points and found that altitude was the main differentiating factor.

tree.answer: Seasonal variability and altitude dependence of fog-water collection along the Mediterranean Iberian coast
Yes, fog-water volumes are measured directly by collectors after a rain filter
Characterize seasonal behaviour, dry-day potential and the altitude effect
No explicit rivals; confounders (exposure, wind) handled by matching sites
Conditions found: site pairs chosen in nature to differ mainly in elevation

tree.question: 6b
tree.answer: Yes: repeated seasons over up to 10 years and five site groups
Volume-altitude relation holds at three more areas; fog-day relation fails at Peñones
Altitude kept as main differentiating factor; day-frequency claim weakened

end.claim: Among nearby collectors with equal exposure to prevailing winds, a larger positive elevation difference gives larger fog-water volumes and more fog days, with the differences largest in summer.

decisive_move.sentence: Installing collector pairs matched in orientation and wind exposure but differing in elevation at Montseny and Muela made the altitude comparison possible.

gates.evidence: The paired Montseny and Muela collectors were installed specifically to test elevation, with matching fixed by design before the data were collected (p. 1940). The seasonal and dry-day analyses mine the existing network data without a guiding hypothesis. The altitude claim could have failed and did partly fail for fog-day frequency at Peñones (p. 1952). No significance tests or preregistered thresholds are reported.

imports.item: coefficient of variation as a relative measure of interannual variability
high-density polyethylene Raschel shade mesh as fog-collection material

novelty_claims.quote: This study aimed to extend the knowledge acquired in the works of Estrela et al. (2008) and Estrela et al. (2019) by analysing some aspects
Although the literature also describes time series for collected fog and mentions its seasonal nature, long seasonal series are hard to find.

limits: Headline: altitude-volume regularity (regularity_in_range). Sub-claims: seasonal pattern, with spring and autumn peaks in volume and summer and autumn peaks in days (regularity_in_range, with record lengths differing by station and no trends detectable); dry-day collection potential (estimate without stated uncertainty, i.e. descriptive). No uncertainty, significance tests or error bars accompany the altitude ratios. The trend analysis is mentioned but not shown (p. 1951). The altitude effect rests on two designed pairs plus three opportunistic groups; matching of exposure is asserted, not quantified. The ratios are internally inconsistent: about sixfold in the abstract and p. 1947 versus 5:1 in the conclusions; 73% more days versus 1.7:1. The text attributes 428 m to Bujete as well as Sierra Helada (p. 1943), apparently an error. The data overlap with Estrela et al. (2019), so the extension is not fully independent. The acknowledgements mention reviewers, but no review file was supplied, so no review sequence is coded. The mechanisms (Azores High, dissipation, liquid water content) are interpretive and untested here (inference).

disagreements.target: Estrela et al. (2019), seasonal frequency from a 1-year (2011) series
disagreements.support: The paper repeats the seasonal analysis with series of up to almost 10 years to obtain more consistent results.
disagreements.quote: Seasonal variability was detected by Estrela et al. (2019) with data from 2011 and for the same fog collectors

disagreements.target: Schemenauer and Cereceda (1994), optimal collector altitude of 400–1,000 m.a.s.l.
disagreements.support: Low sites below 500 m collected less, and the paper suggests about 1,200 m is desirable in the northern and prelittoral parts of the study area.
disagreements.quote: Conversely, this study reveals that the desirable altitude for the north and prelittoral parts of the study area would be around 1,200 m.a.s.l.

alternatives_considered.chosen: Dry-day threshold of 1 mm of precipitation
alternatives_considered.alternatives: The rain sensor's finer resolution (0.2 mm)
alternatives_considered.reason: WMO criteria and recent works; fog droplets captured by rain gauges would record erroneous rain

alternatives_considered.chosen: Only the stations with the longest data series for the CV and frequency-intensity analyses
alternatives_considered.reason: to attain a more significant study
